title: Normalized tensor multiplication from etale quotient stalks
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $T$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use ordinary module sheaves over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on a small representative of $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $E,D\subseteq |T|$ be subsets and let
$$q:A_T\twoheadrightarrow F,\qquad s:A_T\twoheadrightarrow G,\qquad r:A_T\twoheadrightarrow H$$
be epimorphisms of $A_T$-module sheaves. Assume $F$ is flat, meaning tensoring with $F$ preserves short exact sequences [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every geometric point $\bar t$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], assume given $A$-linear identifications
$$F_{\bar t}\cong\begin{cases}A&t\in E,\\0&t\notin E,\end{cases}\qquad
G_{\bar t}\cong\begin{cases}A&t\in D,\\0&t\notin D,\end{cases}\qquad
H_{\bar t}\cong\begin{cases}A&t\in E\cap D,\\0&t\notin E\cap D.\end{cases}$$
Under these identifications the stalk maps of $q,s,r$ are the identity of $A$ on their respective subsets and the zero map otherwise. Use sheaf tensor over $A_T$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and let
$$m:A_T\xrightarrow{\lambda^{-1}}A_T\otimes_{A_T}A_T\xrightarrow{q\otimes s}F\otimes_{A_T}G,$$
where $\lambda(a\otimes b)=ab$. Then $m$ is epic and there is a unique morphism $e:F\otimes_{A_T}G\to H$ with $e\circ m=r$. This morphism is an isomorphism and, for local sections $a,b$ of $A_T$, satisfies
$$e(q(a)\otimes s(b))=r(ab).$$
At $t\in E\cap D$ its stalk is $A\otimes_A A\to A$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, with inverse $c\mapsto c\otimes1$; outside $E\cap D$ it is the unique map $0\to0$.

source.place: Tag 03PU, label theorem-exactness-stalks; agent-formulated normalized quotient-tensor criterion refining the support-quotient argument, not the statement of this tag alone.

proof.text: First fix the tensor convention without changing the quotient maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-constant-ring-module-equivalence], regard an $A_T$-module sheaf as an $A$-module-valued sheaf by scalar restriction, with the same underlying abelian sheaf. Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] to the constant ring presheaf $U\mapsto A$ and these two scalar-restricted sheaves: their module sheafifications are the original $A_T$-module sheaves, and the displayed isomorphism identifies their tensor over $A_T$ with the sheafification of $U\mapsto F(U)\otimes_A G(U)$. This identification sends the image of $x\otimes y$ to the image of that same pure tensor. It respects maps by the cited naturality. Its unit identification sends $a\otimes b$ to $ab$: both maps have this formula before sheafification. Hence the constant-coefficient tensor convention of the geometric-stalk lemma below applies to the tensor and $m$ of the item.

source.place: Tag 0GMW, label lemma-sheafification-tensor; apply to the constant ring presheaf. Agent specialization to the supplied quotient maps.

proof.text: Put $B=F\otimes_{A_T}G$. By [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar](1), $(B)_{\bar t}=F_{\bar t}\otimes_A G_{\bar t}$ naturally, with pure tensor germs and the unit identified as in step 1. Thus $m_{\bar t}$ sends $c$ to $q_{\bar t}(c)\otimes s_{\bar t}(1)$. If $t\in E\cap D$, this is $c\mapsto c\otimes1$ in $A\otimes_A A$. Multiplication $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$ is its inverse, since $(ab)\otimes1=a\otimes b$ by the balancing relation and $c\cdot1=c$. If $t\notin E\cap D$, at least one tensor factor is zero; every pure tensor is then zero, so $B_{\bar t}=0$ and $m_{\bar t}:A\to0$. Consequently every $m_{\bar t}$ is surjective. Its kernel is zero on $E\cap D$ and all of $A$ elsewhere, exactly the kernel of $r_{\bar t}$.

source.place: Tags 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact) and 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks); tensor compatibility via sites-modules Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback). Agent quotient-kernel argument.

proof.text: The category of module sheaves is abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-module-category-abelian], since the site here is small. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1), forgetting to abelian sheaves preserves kernels and cokernels; compose it with the exact stalk functor of [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]. If a module sheaf $M$ has all stalks zero, the underlying map $M\to0$ is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], so $M=0$. This also detects zero morphisms: the image of a map zero on all stalks has all stalks zero by exactness, hence is zero, and the map is zero. Now take $C=\operatorname{coker}(m)$ in the module category. Exactness gives $C_{\bar t}=\operatorname{coker}(m_{\bar t})=0$ by step 2, whence $C=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-preadditive-epi-iff-cokernel-zero], $m$ is an epimorphism.

source.place: Tags 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact) and 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks); tensor compatibility via sites-modules Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback). Agent quotient-kernel argument.

proof.text: Let $k:K\hookrightarrow A_T$ be the kernel of $m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] and [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], $K_{\bar t}\to A$ is the kernel of $m_{\bar t}$. For $t\in E\cap D$, step 2 gives $K_{\bar t}=0$, so $(r\circ k)_{\bar t}=0$. Outside the intersection $r_{\bar t}=0$, so again $(r\circ k)_{\bar t}=0$. The zero-morphism test proved in step 3 using [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] gives $r\circ k=0$. This uses the normalization of the quotient maps, rather than just the abstract isomorphism types of their stalks.

source.place: Tags 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact) and 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks); tensor compatibility via sites-modules Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback). Agent quotient-kernel argument.

proof.text: By the definition of $k$, the complex $K\xrightarrow{k}A_T\xrightarrow{m}B$ is exact at $A_T$. Step 3 makes its second map epic and step 4 gives $r\circ k=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel](a), with $h=k$, the epimorphism $m$, and $\varphi=r$. It produces a unique $A_T$-linear morphism $e:B\to H$ with $e\circ m=r$. Equivalently, uniqueness follows by cancellation of the epimorphism $m$.

source.place: Tags 0109 (definition-abelian-category) and 010E (definition-exact); cokernel descent along an epimorphism, as stated in lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel(a). Agent specialization.

proof.text: At a geometric point in $E\cap D$, the equation $e_{\bar t}\circ m_{\bar t}=r_{\bar t}$ reads $e_{\bar t}(c\otimes1)=c$. Every pure tensor is $(ab)\otimes1=a\otimes b$, so $e_{\bar t}(a\otimes b)=ab$. This is the inverse from step 2, with inverse $c\mapsto c\otimes1$. Off the intersection both $B_{\bar t}$ and $H_{\bar t}$ are zero, so $e_{\bar t}$ is the unique map $0\to0$, an isomorphism. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to the underlying abelian map of $e$: it is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. Its inverse is $A_T$-linear: for $a\in A_T(U)$ and $h\in H(U)$, write $h=e_U(b)$; then $e_U(ab)=a h$, so $e_U^{-1}(a h)=a e_U^{-1}(h)$. Thus $e$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves, with exactly the asserted stalk normalization.

source.place: Tags 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact) and 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks); tensor compatibility via sites-modules Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback). Agent quotient-kernel argument.

proof.text: For any object $U$ of the etale site and $a,b\in A_T(U)$, the tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives $q(a)\otimes s(b)=ab\,(q(1)\otimes s(1))=m(ab)$ as sections of $B$ over $U$. Here the equality follows from $A_T(U)$-bilinearity before sheafification and hence remains true after sheafification. Applying $e$ and $e\circ m=r$ yields $e(q(a)\otimes s(b))=r(ab)$. This finishes every clause, including the epic generator, uniqueness, section formula and stalk inverse. The assumed flatness is compatible with the proof but is not needed by this argument.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q119-3183173e7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: This is a first proof of a statement-only node created by Q57; there is no re-split repair note. The statement and stmt_deps are identical to live, where the item is unsplit, and flatness is kept although unused. There are 0 new nodes. Each of the 7 steps checked against the statements it cites. (1) Constant-ring equivalence plus lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor (second clause) identify ⊗_{A_T} with the sheafified ⊗_A presheaf. (2) pod stalk-tensor (1) gives m_t(c)=q_t(c)⊗s_t(1): this is c↦c⊗1 on E∩D, with multiplication as its inverse, and B_t=0 elsewhere. (3) Module sheaves form an abelian category, and the exact faithful forgetful functor, exact stalks and conservativity give coker m=0, so m is epic. (4) r∘k has zero stalks, so it is zero. (5) The exact-epi cokernel lemma (a) gives the unique e. (6) e is an isomorphism by stalks plus conservativity, and the inverse is A_T-linear. (7) The section formula follows from bilinearity (elementary). Small cases tested: T empty, A=0, E=D=|T|, E∩D empty, and the asymmetric points. Sources checked: Stacks 03PU/03PT (etale-cohomology.tex l.3546/3456) and the sites-modules lemma-sheafification-tensor; no SGA source. Duplicate search over dag/nodes found no match; lem-sfb-integral-tensor-quotient-epimorphism is a different statement. The tool_uses are generic and accepted. Batch-5 flag on lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar: it is generic sheaf algebra. Its 66-node closure contains no trace-formula node and no PD proof node; the only other pod node is def-pod-ring-scalar-extension. Accepted.
